## Foundations of Clinical Research — From Clinical Question to Publication

**Provider:** Neudata · **#ClearDataClearImpact**


* * *

## Welcome

Every day you make clinical decisions that research could improve. Over **four weekends** this course walks the whole road of research with you: from a question at the bedside, to a sound study design, to analysing data, to writing and publishing the paper.

You do not need any research or statistics background. We go **slowly**, with pictures, examples from your own wards and a lot of group work. You will never be asked to calculate anything beyond a simple 2×2 table, and you do not need any software: the trainers run the analyses, and you learn to read and write them up.

## The course at a glance

| Weekend | Session | Theme | Your group builds |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | 1 · Saturday | **ASK** — from clinical problem to research question | Proposal: topic, PICO, question, aims |
| | 2 · Sunday | **FIND & READ** — searching, managing references, reading a paper in 15 minutes | Proposal: search, 5 references, problem statement, working title |
| **2** | 3 · Saturday | **DESIGN** — choosing the right study | Proposal: design, setting, population |
| | 4 · Sunday | **BIAS & EFFECT** — bias, confounding, RR/OR/NNT, diagnostic tests, forest plots | Proposal: exposure, outcomes, bias plan |
| **3** | 5 · Saturday | **DATA** — CRFs, data management, describing data; *meet the course dataset* | Proposal: variables, CRF, data plan · Manuscript: Table 1 understood |
| | 6 · Sunday | **ANALYSE** — CIs, p-values, tests, regression, survival, missing data; *analyse the course dataset* | Proposal: sample size, analysis plan · Manuscript: results interpreted |
| **4** | 7 · Saturday | **PROTECT & WRITE** — ethics, registration, integrity; writing Methods and Results | Proposal: ethics, feasibility, publication plan · Manuscript: Methods + Results |
| | 8 · Sunday | **PUBLISH** — Introduction, Discussion, abstract; journals, submission, peer review; presentations | Manuscript: complete draft · Proposal presented |

Each session lasts **3 hours with a 15-minute break**: a short recap, two teaching blocks with frequent "check your understanding" moments, and time to build your proposal or paper. Each session also has **extra slides** at the end for anyone who wants to read further at home.

### The running example
One clinical topic travels with us: **fluids in septic shock**. In Weekends 1–2 we ask, search and design the question, and look at two real papers (a randomised trial and a cohort study). In Weekends 3–4 we analyse **FLUID-ICU**, a realistic *simulated* dataset of 620 ICU patients, and write it up as a paper.

## Your group and its two products

You stay in the **same group of about six** for all eight sessions. Agree roles in Session 1 (they can rotate): facilitator, scribe, timekeeper, literature lead, methods & data lead, presenter.

1. **A research proposal on your own question**, built one part per weekend and **presented in Session 8** (6 minutes + 2 minutes of feedback). See `Assignment/proposal_brief.md`.
2. **A draft manuscript from the course dataset.** Each group answers a different question on FLUID-ICU (e.g. fluid balance and mortality, kidney injury, ventilator-free days, lactate and missing data, ICU length of stay), using its **results pack**. You draft Methods and Results in Session 7 and the rest in Session 8. After the course, groups **review each other's drafts and reply like real authors**. See `Assignment/manuscript_brief.md` and `Assignment/peer_review_instructions.md`.

## Between sessions (about 30–60 minutes)

| After | Do this |
|---|---|
| Session 1 | Think of synonyms for your PICO terms |
| Session 2 | Finish Proposal Part 1 and the literature matrix; read the abstract of Paper 2 |
| Weekend 2 | Finish Proposal Part 2 |
| Session 5 | Read your group's results pack (Table 1 and figures) |
| Weekend 3 | Finish Proposal Part 3; read Papers 1 and 2; start your 6-slide presentation |
| Session 7 | Finish Proposal Part 4 and your presentation; re-read your Methods + Results |
| Session 8 | Polish the manuscript; peer-review swap and response letter within **2 weeks** |

## What you need
A pen, a notebook, and (optional) a laptop or phone for PubMed and the online quiz. No software to install. Participants who have done the free Neudata course *Clinical Data Analysis in R* may re-run the course analyses with the scripts in `Data/R/`.

## The quiz
In Session 1 and again at the end of Session 8 you answer the same 24 questions. It is anonymous (participant number only) and measures what the **course** achieved, not you.

## After the course
Take your proposal to the ethics committee, keep improving your manuscript, and — if you want to run analyses yourself — follow the free *Clinical Data Analysis in R* course and the optional advanced modules (`Advanced_Modules/`).
